title: Sindhu, Satwik-Chirag, and a New Generation. India Has Named Its Strongest Badminton Squad for the Asian Games.
excerpt: BAI’s 20-member roster for Aichi-Nagoya blends proven champions with rising stars like Ayush Shetty and Unnati Hooda, as Indian badminton chases its best-ever continental campaign
body:
She won Olympic medals in Rio and Tokyo and two Asian Games bronzes in Jakarta and Hangzhou. Now PV Sindhu is heading to Aichi-Nagoya in September as the face of an Indian badminton squad that blends proven champions with a generation of players who were still in their teens when Sindhu first made India a force on the global circuit.

The Badminton Association of India announced a 20-member squad on Saturday for the 2026 Asian Games, to be held in Japan from September 19 to October 4. It is a roster built to defend and extend the gains of the 2022 edition in Hangzhou, where India recorded its best-ever badminton performance at the continental Games: one gold, one silver, and an individual bronze.

## The headliners

Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, whose 2022 gold medal in men’s doubles rewrote the script for Indian badminton, return as the pair to beat. Their resurgence after a brief dip — back among the world’s top doubles combinations and fresh off a Thomas Cup bronze medal earlier this year — means they arrive with form and pedigree.

In men’s singles, Lakshya Sen leads the charge. The 24-year-old has climbed back into the world’s top 10 after a frustrating 2024 and will be joined by Ayush Shetty, whose silver medal at the Badminton Asia Championships marked him out as a serious prospect. Experienced campaigners H. S. Prannoy and Kidambi Srikanth round out a men’s team that secured a silver in the team event at the last Asian Games.

On the women’s side, Sindhu anchors the singles alongside Unnati Hooda, a BWF World Junior Championships medallist who represents the new generation of Indian shuttlers. Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand Pullela continue to lead India’s women’s doubles challenge. Mixed doubles will feature the increasingly sharp pairing of Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto.

## Youth movement

What makes this squad distinctive is not the star names — those were always going to be there — but the depth behind them. Devika Sihag, a Thailand Masters Super 300 champion, and Tharun Mannepalli add singles depth. Hariharan Amsakarunan and M. R. Arjun form a second men’s doubles pair with genuine international credentials. And in women’s doubles, Kavipriya Selvam and Simran Singhi offer BAI a second competitive combination alongside the established Treesa-Gayatri partnership.

“Indian badminton today is in a position where success is being shaped not just by individual excellence, but by the growing depth of talent across categories,” BAI General Secretary Sanjay Mishra said. “This squad reflects that journey — a blend of experience, depth and emerging talent.”

The selection committee finalised the squad based on recent performances at national and international tournaments, alongside BWF rankings as of May 26, 2026.

## Why this matters for the diaspora

Badminton has always occupied a peculiar space in the Indian sporting imagination — massive participation at the amateur level, particularly among communities in the US, UK, and Canada, but historically short on global results. That changed with Sindhu’s Olympic medals, Saina Nehwal’s trailblazing a decade earlier, and the Satwik-Chirag revolution in doubles.

For NRIs in the US, the Aichi-Nagoya timing is significant. The 13-hour time difference with the East Coast means prime-time matches in Japan will air early morning in America — far more accessible than European or Middle Eastern tournament hours. And with India competing across all five individual disciplines at the Games, there will be no shortage of matches to track.

The Asian Games have traditionally been India’s best platform for multi-sport medal hauls, and badminton has emerged as one of the most reliable contributors. At the 2022 edition, the sport delivered three of India’s 107 total medals. With this squad, BAI is betting it can match or exceed that tally in Japan.

India’s 13 Asian Games medals in badminton history are already the most by a South Asian nation. In Aichi-Nagoya, the ambition is to add to that count with a squad that, for the first time, has genuine contenders in every discipline on the draw sheet.
